नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा तथा ऊर्जा दक्षता सम्बन्धी विधेयक, २०८३

ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत तथा सिँचाइ मन्त्रालय · Hon. Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha · House of Representatives, Session तेस्रो

Bill document (PDF)

Summary

Bill detail

The name of this bill is the "Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 7). The main purpose of this bill is to identify, promote, develop, and expand renewable energy to contribute to environmental protection, increase citizens' access to energy, and achieve sustainable development through energy efficiency, saving, and conservation (Preamble, Page 7). This Act shall come into force on the thirty-first day from the date of certification (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 7). The responsibility to identify, promote, develop, and expand renewable energy to increase citizens' access belongs to the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, and local levels (Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 8). The three levels of government must cooperate and coordinate with each other to provide energy access to citizens (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 9). All three levels of government may take technical or other assistance from the Center to run projects or programs related to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy conservation (Section 3, Subsection 4, Page 9). To achieve energy efficiency and energy conservation, the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, and local levels must fulfill responsibilities and obligations to prepare and implement programs according to policies and standards, use and cause to use efficient technology and equipment when using energy, discourage unnecessary energy use, implement programs supporting proper energy use and management, prioritize and promote energy-efficient technology, equipment, and services, implement environmental protection and sustainable development measures in energy production, development, and use, and raise public awareness (Section 6, Subsection 1, Page 10). Business establishments or sectors listed in the Schedule that consume energy in quantities determined by the Government of Nepal must fulfill designated obligations to achieve energy efficiency and energy conservation (Section 6, Subsection 2, Page 10). The business establishments or sectors listed in the Schedule include businesses, industries, factories, and commercial establishments, passenger and non-passenger transport vehicles, government, commercial, residential, and trade buildings, service sectors such as hospitals, schools, and universities, agriculture, irrigation, and drinking water sectors, energy production, supply, or consumption equipment, its production or import, and energy production, transmission, or distribution (Schedule, Page 27). Business establishments or sectors must fulfill obligations to prepare and implement annual targets, plans, and programs for energy efficiency and conservation, keep monthly records and logs of energy consumption, use energy-efficient technology and equipment, prepare and implement an annual action plan and targets to replace high energy-consuming technology and equipment, conduct energy audits, and implement recommendations of energy audit reports (Section 6, Subsection 2, Page 10-11). To execute these obligations, business establishments or sectors must arrange for an energy manager (Section 6, Subsection 3, Page 11). Operating business establishments or sectors must have an energy audit conducted by an energy auditor within three years for the first time after coming into operation, and every three years thereafter (Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 11). Business establishments or sectors operating at the time of commencement of this Act must have an energy audit conducted by an energy auditor for the first time within three years from the date of commencement of this Act (Section 7, Subsection 2, Page 11). Business establishments or sectors must participate in the energy saving scheme formulated by the Center (Section 9, Subsection 3, Page 12). A business establishment or sector that cannot achieve its energy saving target must purchase energy saving certificates from other business establishments or sectors that save energy beyond their target to complete the target, and if it fails to complete the target by purchasing certificates, it must pay compensation to the Center (Section 9, Subsections 6 and 7, Page 12-13). To generate, transmit, or distribute electricity from renewable energy sources, the concerned person, institution, or body must obtain a license according to prevailing law (Section 5, Page 9). A person wishing to work as an energy auditor must obtain an energy auditor license from the Center, for which the person must have a Bachelor's degree or equivalent in engineering or energy-related subjects from a recognized university, at least two years of experience in the energy sector, and completed training conducted by the Center (Section 8, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 11). The Center shall grant an energy auditor license for five years by prescribing necessary conditions, and it must be renewed before expiry by paying the prescribed fee (Section 8, Subsections 3 and 4, Page 11). If not renewed within that period, it may be renewed within six months from the date of expiry by paying an additional prescribed fee (Section 8, Subsection 5, Page 12). The Government of Nepal may determine quality standards for technologies, appliances, or equipment related to renewable energy and energy efficiency by publishing a notice in the Nepal Gazette (Section 26, Page 20). Any person, institution, or body wishing to sell or distribute technologies, appliances, or equipment in Nepal must get them tested by the Center by paying the prescribed service fee (Section 27, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 20-21). If testing shows excessive energy consumption, the Committee may recommend to the Government of Nepal to prohibit or ban its production, export, import, or sale, and on that basis, the Government of Nepal may prohibit or ban it (Section 28, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 21). The Center shall establish and operate a laboratory to test whether quality standards are met, and until the laboratory is established, quality testing may be done at a laboratory designated by the Government of Nepal through a notice in the Nepal Gazette (Section 29, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 21). The Center shall issue energy saving certificates to business establishments or sectors that save energy beyond their targets, which can be sold or purchased (Section 9, Subsections 4 and 6, Pages 12-13). The Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Center is established to identify, promote, develop, and expand renewable energy, and to achieve energy efficiency and energy conservation, which shall be an autonomous and corporate body with perpetual succession (Section 10, Subsection 1, Page 13; Section 11, Subsection 1, Page 13). The central office of the Center shall be located in the Kathmandu Valley (Section 10, Subsection 3, Page 13). The main functions, duties, and powers of the Center include preparing policies, strategies, plans, and programs related to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and conservation, implementing or causing the implementation of approved plans and programs, providing technical and other assistance to all three levels of government and other bodies to run projects, implementing projects supporting the energy mix, encouraging private sector participation and investment growth, promoting research and development, use, promotion, and testing of new technologies, preparing training curricula for energy auditors, supporting the Government of Nepal in implementing international commitments, collecting and analyzing data, and developing and implementing projects related to carbon emission reduction and climate adaptation for carbon trade growth (Section 12, Pages 13-14). To operate, supervise, and manage the activities of the Center, there shall be a 13-member Board of Directors consisting of the Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation as Chairperson, Secretary of the Ministry, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Finance, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Environment, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Joint Secretary (Law) of the Ministry, Executive Director of the Nepal Electricity Authority, three members nominated by the Ministry representing renewable energy producers and consumers including at least one woman, President of the Municipal Association of Nepal or representative, President of the National Association of Rural Municipalities in Nepal or representative as members, and the Chief Executive Officer as Member-Secretary (Section 14, Subsection 1, Pages 14-15). The term of office of nominated members shall be three years and they may be re-nominated once (Section 14, Subsection 3, Page 15). There shall be a Chief Executive Officer to work as the executive head of the Center, who shall be appointed by the Government of Nepal, Council of Ministers for a term of four years through open competition upon recommendation of a recommendation committee (Section 17, Subsections 1, 3, 5, and 6, Pages 16-17). To be eligible as Chief Executive Officer, a person must be a Nepali citizen, not exceeding sixty years of age, holding at least a Master's degree in environmental science, engineering, energy, science, management, finance, or economics from a recognized university, and having at least ten years of work experience at a managerial or officer level in the field of renewable energy, energy efficiency, or energy conservation (Section 18, Page 17). There shall be a separate fund named the Sustainable Energy Fund in the Center, which shall include amounts received from the Government of Nepal, individuals or institutions, foreign grants received with the approval of the Ministry of Finance, service fees, amounts from carbon trade and climate finance, license and renewal fees, and compensation amounts, and the fund's money shall be deposited in a Class 'A' commercial bank (Section 30, Subsections 1, 2, 3, and 4, Pages 21-22). If anyone fails to fulfill responsibilities and obligations under Section 6 Subsection (2), the Chief Executive Officer shall impose a fine of up to Rs. 5 lakh (Section 32, Subsection 1 Clause (a), Page 22). If anyone sells or distributes technology, appliances, or equipment required to be tested under Section 27 Subsection (1) without testing, the Chief Executive Officer shall impose a fine of up to Rs. 10 lakh (Section 32, Subsection 1 Clause (b), Page 22). If anyone manufactures, exports, imports, or sells or distributes technology, appliances, or equipment prohibited or banned under Section 28 Subsection (2), the Chief Executive Officer shall impose a fine of up to Rs. 20 lakh (Section 32, Subsection 1 Clause (c), Page 22). If technical or other assistance received from the Center is misused contrary to purpose, the Chief Executive Officer shall impose a fine as specified in the agreement if an agreement exists, or if no agreement exists, shall recover the claimed amount and impose a fine equal to the claimed amount (Section 32, Subsection 1 Clause (d), Page 23). If anyone commits any act contrary to this Act other than these, the Chief Executive Officer shall impose a fine of up to Rs. 3 lakh (Section 32, Subsection 1 Clause (e), Page 23). The power to impose fines is given to the Chief Executive Officer, and a reasonable opportunity to present defense must be given before imposing a fine (Section 32, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 22-23). Any person, institution, or body dissatisfied with the fine imposed by the Chief Executive Officer may appeal to the concerned District Court within thirty-five days from the date of receiving information of the decision (Section 32, Subsection 3, Page 23). This Act repeals the Alternative Energy Development Committee (Formation) Order, 2053 (Section 48, Subsection 1, Page 26). The Alternative Energy Promotion Centre established under the said Order shall automatically convert into the Center after the commencement of this Act (Section 48, Subsection 2, Page 26). All movable and immovable assets and liabilities of the committee formed under the repealed Order shall transfer to the Center (Section 48, Subsection 4, Page 26). The Central Renewable Energy Fund under the said Order shall automatically convert into the fund under this Act (Section 48, Subsection 5, Page 26). Permanent employees working in the committee formed under the repealed Order shall be deemed to be serving in equivalent levels and posts of the Center (Section 48, Subsection 6, Page 26). The Executive Director appointed and serving under the repealed Order at the time of commencement of this Act shall remain in office for his remaining term of office (Section 48, Subsection 7, Page 26).
